nodes.name: Alpine grasses & sedges
nodes.desc: Short-turf meadow plants above the treeline, grazed by wild and domestic hoofed animals and by marmots.

nodes.name: Alpine wildflowers
nodes.desc: Gentians, primroses and buttercups that marmots eat, along with other flowering plants of the high meadows.

nodes.name: Rhododendron
nodes.desc: Shrubs that dominate the slopes at roughly 4,000 to 5,000 m together with juniper, according to Wikipedia on the park.

nodes.name: Fir and juniper
nodes.desc: Conifers of the subalpine forest, which Wikipedia says holds fir, birch and rhododendron above about 3,000 m.

nodes.name: Lichens & mosses
nodes.desc: Hardy growth that survives above 5,000 m, and food for musk deer in winter.

nodes.name: Himalayan tahr
nodes.desc: Grazes grasses and browses shrubs on steep rocky slopes, moving downslope in winter. Snow leopards prey on it.

nodes.name: Blue sheep (bharal)
nodes.desc: A grazer of alpine meadows and rocky slopes. It is the favoured prey of snow leopards, and wolves also hunt it.

nodes.name: Alpine musk deer
nodes.desc: A shy browser of herbs, shrub leaves, mosses and lichens in high conifer and shrub forest.

nodes.name: Himalayan marmot
nodes.desc: Colonial burrowing grazer of alpine grassland. Snow leopards, wolves, red foxes and golden eagles hunt it.

nodes.name: Large-eared pika
nodes.desc: A small lagomorph of rocky high slopes that eats grasses and herbs. Predators here are inferred from general knowledge.

nodes.name: Yak
nodes.desc: Grazing livestock herded in the high valleys, which overlap heavily with wild herbivores for pasture.

nodes.name: Himalayan snowcock
nodes.desc: A large alpine game bird that feeds on plants on open high slopes, and lives in the park per Wikipedia.

nodes.name: Himalayan monal
nodes.desc: Digs through snow for tubers, shoots and some insects in forest and alpine meadows, moving down in winter.

nodes.name: Lammergeier (bearded vulture)
nodes.desc: Lives on bone, mostly 85 to 90 percent of an adult's diet, and drops big bones from the air to crack them.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: Large raptor that takes marmots and, from general knowledge, pikas and game birds.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A small predator of marmots and, from general knowledge, pikas.

nodes.name: Snow leopard
nodes.desc: Himalayan apex predator that lives above about 3,500 m. Blue sheep are its core prey, with tahr, musk deer and marmots also taken.

nodes.name: Himalayan wolf
nodes.desc: Hunts bharal and marmots, and takes livestock where herds overlap its range.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong high-altitude light drives a short growing season.

nodes.name: Snowmelt and glacier meltwater
nodes.desc: Meltwater from snowfields and glaciers feeds meadows and streams in spring and summer.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Summer monsoon rain waters the lower slopes and forests.

nodes.name: Thin mountain soil
nodes.desc: Cold, thin soils slow plant growth and nutrient release.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses, slowly in the cold, returning nutrients.
